1.s: Paul praises their growing faith under persecution and assures them God will set things right when Jesus is revealed.
1.d: God will give his suffering people relief and judge those who persecute the church [[tosn:2 Thessalonians 1:3-10]] [[tosn:2 Thessalonians 1:7]].

2.s: The day of the Lord has not yet come; first “the man of sin” must be revealed. Stand firm in the teaching you received.
2.d: Before the day of the Lord, a great rebellion will come and the man of lawlessness will be revealed [[tosn:2 Thessalonians 2:1-12]]. Who or what is “restraining him” [[bible:2 Thessalonians 2:6]] is not known: suggestions include God, the Holy Spirit, the church, the gospel, Paul, and the Roman emperor or empire [[tosn:2 Thessalonians 2:6]].

3.s: Pray for us. Keep away from those who refuse to work: “If anyone is not willing to work, don’t let him eat.” “don’t be weary in doing what is right.”
3.d: Paul takes the pen to add a greeting in his own hand, “the sign in every letter” [[tosn:2 Thessalonians 3:17]] [[bible:2 Thessalonians 3:17]].
